job_statement: When planning to upgrade to OpenShift Pipelines 1.17, I want to understand the removal of ClusterTask resources and migration path to cluster resolver, so I can prepare my pipelines for the breaking change and avoid failures after upgrade.
prerequisites: Understanding current pipeline definitions using ClusterTask

evidence.content: With this update, the deprecated `ClusterTask` resource is removed from the Operator. As an alternative, you can use the cluster resolver to access tasks that {pipelines-shortname} installs in the `openshift-pipelines` namespace.

job_statement: When I have pipelines using deprecated ClusterTask resources, I want to understand how to use the cluster resolver to access tasks in the openshift-pipelines namespace, so I can migrate my pipelines before upgrading to version 1.17.
desired_outcomes: Successful migration from ClusterTask to cluster resolver

evidence.content: Before upgrading to {pipelines-shortname} 1.17, if you configured any pipelines that use `ClusterTask` resources, you must edit them to use the tasks in the `openshift-pipelines` namespace.

job_statement: When managing multiple Git providers in my CI/CD infrastructure, I want to understand how the new Git resolver multi-configuration capability works, so I can consolidate my Git provider management and streamline pipeline definitions.
desired_outcomes: Understanding of multi-Git provider configuration pattern
Awareness of configuration organization in TektonConfig CR

evidence.content: With this release, you can configure multiple Git providers by using the Git resolver, or you can add multiple configurations for the same Git provider, in the `TektonConfig` custom resource (CR).

job_statement: When I need to reference tasks from different Git providers in my pipeline runs, I want to understand how to specify the configKey parameter, so I can select the appropriate Git configuration for each task or pipeline run.
desired_outcomes: Ability to select specific Git configurations

evidence.content: Example of using a `test1` configuration in a pipeline run

job_statement: When monitoring pipeline execution in my OpenShift cluster, I want to understand the new granular monitoring levels for PipelineRun resources, so I can choose the appropriate monitoring scope for my operational needs.
desired_outcomes: Understanding of monitoring levels (cluster, namespace, pipeline, pipelinerun)
Knowledge of trade-offs between monitoring granularity
Awareness of configuration options in TektonConfig

evidence.content: With this update, you can now monitor the running `PipelineRun` resources at the namespace, pipeline, and pipeline runlevel, in addition to the cluster level.

job_statement: When I need namespace-level monitoring for PipelineRun resources, I want to understand how to configure the metrics.running-pipelinerun.level parameter, so I can implement the appropriate monitoring granularity.

evidence.content: You can configure the level through the `TektonConfig` custom resource by setting the `metrics.running-pipelinerun.level` parameter value to `namespace`, `pipeline`, or `pipelinerun`.

job_statement: When using Tekton Chains for artifact signing, I want to understand the new ecdsa key pair generation capability and default configuration changes, so I can ensure proper artifact signing without manual configuration.
desired_outcomes: Understanding of ecdsa key pair generation
Knowledge of signing secret generation options

evidence.content: With this update, you can configure the `TektonConfig` custom resource (CR) to generate the `x509` key pair of the `ecdsa` type and use it with {tekton-chains} to sign artifacts.

job_statement: When I want to enable automatic signing secret generation, I want to understand how the generateSigningSecret field works, so I can configure Tekton Chains without manually creating key pairs.
desired_outcomes: Successful enabling of automatic key generation

evidence.content: You can generate the key pair by setting the `generateSigningSecret` field in the `TektonConfig` custom resource (CR) to `true`

job_statement: When I do not explicitly configure Tekton Chains in TektonConfig, I want to understand what default configuration the Operator applies, so I can assess whether the defaults meet my security and storage requirements.
desired_outcomes: Knowledge of default artifact formats and storage
Awareness of behavior change from previous versions

evidence.content: Before this update, if you did not configure {tekton-chains} in the `TektonConfig` CR, the Operator would not pass any default Chains configuration. With this update, if you do not configure {tekton-chains} in the `TektonConfig` CR, the Operator sets the {tekton-chains} configuration with these default properties

job_statement: When using Pipelines as Code for CI/CD workflows, I want to understand the new metrics for PipelineRun monitoring, so I can track pipeline execution performance and identify bottlenecks.

evidence.content: With this update, the `pipelines_as_code_running_pipelineruns_count` metric is added to show the number of running `PipelineRun` resources in {pac}. The metric can be filtered by repository or by namespace.

job_statement: When I need to monitor running pipeline count in Pipelines as Code, I want to understand the pipelines_as_code_running_pipelineruns_count metric and its filtering options, so I can track concurrent pipeline execution.

evidence.content: the `pipelines_as_code_running_pipelineruns_count` metric is added to show the number of running `PipelineRun` resources in {pac}. The metric can be filtered by repository or by namespace.

job_statement: When I need to analyze pipeline execution duration, I want to understand the pipelines_as_code_pipelinerun_duration_seconds_sum metric and its filtering dimensions, so I can identify slow pipelines and failure patterns.

evidence.content: the `pipelines_as_code_pipelinerun_duration_seconds_sum` metric is added to show the total duration in seconds taken by all `PipelineRun` resources in {pac}. The metric can be filtered by repository, namespace, `PipelineRun` status, and `PipelineRun` status change reason.

job_statement: When evaluating whether to upgrade to OpenShift Pipelines 1.17, I want to understand the removal of community cluster tasks and alternative access methods, so I can plan for obtaining required tasks from external sources.
desired_outcomes: Understanding of Tekton catalog as alternative
Knowledge of future task availability plans

evidence.content: With this update, the community cluster tasks are removed from the Operator. As an alternative, you can download them from the link:https://github.com/tektoncd/catalog[Tekton catalog] (GitHub resource).

job_statement: When my pipelines depend on removed community cluster tasks, I want to understand which specific tasks were removed and how to obtain them from Tekton catalog, so I can maintain pipeline functionality after upgrade.

evidence.content: The following list shows the removed community cluster tasks: argocd-task-sync-and-wait, git-cli, helm-upgrade-from-repo, helm-upgrade-from-source, jib-maven, kubeconfig-creator, pull-request, trigger-jenkins-job

job_statement: When managing Tekton Results for pipeline execution tracking, I want to understand the new summary labels and annotations configuration capability, so I can customize which metadata appears in results tables for easier analysis.
desired_outcomes: Knowledge of label and annotation selection

evidence.content: With this update, you can configure {tekton-results} to include certain labels and annotations from the YAML manifests of pipelines and tasks in the `summary fields` column in the results tables.

job_statement: When troubleshooting pipeline execution issues in OpenShift Pipelines 1.17, I want to understand the key bug fixes related to task run failures and status reporting, so I can verify that previously encountered issues are resolved.
desired_outcomes: Awareness of fixed failure handling issues

evidence.content: With this update, the pipeline run failure handling is fixed to accurately report validation failures in the `status.message` field and consistently trigger `finally` tasks, even if a task fails the validation.

job_statement: When my pipelines use finally tasks for cleanup, I want to understand that finally tasks now run correctly even after validation failures, so I can rely on consistent cleanup execution.

evidence.content: the pipeline run failure handling is fixed to accurately report validation failures in the `status.message` field and consistently trigger `finally` tasks, even if a task fails the validation.

job_statement: When using Pipelines as Code with GitLab repositories containing many files, I want to understand that the 20-file limitation bug is fixed, so I can organize pipeline definitions without execution failures.

evidence.content: Before this update, when using {pac} with GitLab, if the `.tekton` directory contained more than 20 files, some pipeline runs failed to start. With this update, the pipeline runs start correctly.
